claims.text: Victoria has ruled the Empire's living subjects since 1837, so few alive remember any other reign.
For the game the age runs almost two decades, from 1880 to 1897.
It opens with secret masters guiding the founders of the Golden Dawn, and ends when a Transylvanian count reaches London.
Later vampires look back on it as the peak of their hidden civilisation.

title: The Kindred and the Occult Revival
summary: How vampires spread through the secret societies.

claims.text: Mortals start the Golden Dawn in 1880, but Kindred soon infest it and use it to draw living initiates.
From there they spread fast through the secret societies of the age, and the revived occult arts bring both opportunity and terror.

title: Gaslight and Torchlight
summary: The two halves of the Victorian world.

claims.text: The world divides into civilised lands under gaslight and barbarous ones still lit by torches.
In the cities, marble and stone fronts are blackened by industrial soot by day and blood by night; in the barbarous lands vampires sink into humanity's worst nightmares and revel in the old ways.
Vampires of the age act as models of Victorian ideals, as tragic figures or as shameless villains; some seek redemption, others outdo the worst horror tales.

title: Dracula in London
summary: The count who breaks the line between East and West.

claims.text: In 1897 Vlad Dracula arrives in London and whispers a story to an Irish author that strains the Masquerade to its limits.
Dracula sets out to cross from East to West, bringing the old power of the wild lands into the very centre of the civilised world.
When the era closes, the wall between civilised and barbarous worlds is broken, and a century of madness follows.

title: The Sects in the Victorian Age
summary: How the Camarilla and Sabbat look in this era.

claims.text: Two societies define Kindred conflict: the Camarilla and the Sabbat, at war for centuries over politics and philosophy.
To vampires made in this age the two sects stand for Good and Evil; whether that is a fiction of their elders is open to doubt.
Camarilla elders blow up tales of Sabbat crimes, such as raising armies of fresh childer from graveyards or pacts with the Devil, to justify tyranny at home.
Some suspect the drama keeps rulers on both sides in power, and a few whisper of ancients moving both sects like chess pieces.
The Camarilla is said to date from the 15th century, founded to shield vampires from human wrath.

title: Mithras, Prince of London
summary: The long-reigning prince of the Empire's capital.

claims.text: Mithras has been Prince of London for centuries; the childe Valerius conducts much of the nightly business.
The excesses of this princedom set a tradition that lasts well into the next century.
The Antediluvians have faded so far from view that most Kindred doubt they exist, though they live on in vampire legend.

title: History and Mystery
summary: How closely to follow real Victorian history.

claims.text: A troupe may insist on Victorian accuracy or keep only the spirit of the age; both are valid.
This world is not ours but one in the shadow of our past; if events ran exactly as they did in real history, the mystery horror needs would be lost.
The Storyteller should balance close detail against free invention.

title: Brujah in the Victorian Age
summary: A clan sliding to the margins.

claims.text: Young Brujah, used to the rapid change of the age, expect it to carry the same weight with other Kindred, and miss how their taste for sweeping change sets their elders and conservative clans against them.
The clan has fallen from idealistic agents of a new Kindred order to sidelined neonates and bitter elders.

title: Gangrel in the Victorian Age
summary: Close to the Beast, drifting from politics.

claims.text: The Embrace brings Gangrel near the Beast; to offset this some take titles, becoming scourges of a city's outskirts in Camarilla lands or joining the Sabbat's apocalyptic knightly orders.
A few go autarkis and ignore princes altogether; most Gangrel still belong to the Camarilla, though the clan's interest in politics is fading.
As mortals come to see insanity as more than a defect, Kindred too watch the Lunatics with fresh and morbid interest.
Some wonder, borrowing Darwin's language, whether the Malkavians are an evolutionary step in how Caine's line meets the world, or just twisted products of the times.
Where many undead stay frozen, the Nosferatu adapt to the age's changes with unusual speed, unwilling to become relics while Ventrue and Toreador revel in old legacies.
Only the Gangrel hold more sway over animals than they do.
The Toreador may be the best of all Kindred at passing for mortal, keeping close to the fancies of the living.
They work their will through influence and gesture instead of blood and fire, while others dismiss them with narrow stereotypes of dandies.

title: Tremere in the Victorian Age
summary: Sorcerers first, with a fall ahead.

claims.text: The Tremere think of themselves as sorcerers before Kindred, and the birth of psychology fits the clan's swift rise in the period.
By the end of the era, for all its occult leanings, the Tremere are set to be pushed to the margins once more.
Some Ventrue show only greed and a stale sense of entitlement; others stand up for sect and clan against the Sabbat or calmly settle feuds; most fall between.
They hold that without order Kindred would turn on themselves, pointing to the Anarch Revolt and the Inquisition, so a ruling clan must lead others from their self-destructive urges.

title: Lasombra in the Victorian Age
summary: Old ways in a new world.

claims.text: Lasombra customs grow more outdated each night, and the clan must find a workable alternative to stay relevant.
They pick domains that suit refined, showy tastes but where their sins will not be dug up by day by a righteous Inquisition: districts in decline or on the rise, and churches.

title: Tzimisce in the Victorian Age
summary: Feudal lords of the barbarous lands.

claims.text: Most Tzimisce domains sit in the barbarous lands, where Western ideas of government have not reached; some Fiends remain feudal lords in the literal sense.
They keep guards and networks of agents and set local peasants against each other, while most now mark their domains by artificial means.
An Assamite among the Kindred may be a contractor, a paid bodyguard or an adviser, so is not always cause for alarm, though many vampires panic anyway.
In some Camarilla circles they are tolerated, even welcomed; young British and Western Kindred are fascinated by them as exotic.

title: Followers of Set in the Victorian Age

claims.text: Few Setites work in Paris; Adrian King, who holds much power in occult groups across the Empire and Western Europe, has said Parisians already manage what Setites might do there.
Setite strength is growing in America, in New England and along the East Coast.
The clan's elders seem to have a greater goal, with control of the financial markets only a means to it, though most Giovanni are content with the wealth.
Even without necromancy they could be among the strongest clans; only Brujah, Toreador, Ventrue and Lasombra hold wider influence as clans.
Many recent Embraces are not of Gypsy blood; the bond lies in shared outlook instead.
The clan is known for tricksters, deceivers and thieves, and is mostly nomadic, by choice for the most part.
Mithras is older than England itself and has never let go of many pagan ways, though London's Kindred are otherwise refined.
The prince's power seems unchallenged, yet skirmishes over the princedom go on.

title: Lisbon
summary: A city ruled through a voice.

claims.text: Lisbon's Kindred, elders among them, heed a young mortal woman called the Voice of the Prince.
Most assume the Voice speaks for some great power, since a prince in disguise would be too obvious; yet in a sense the Voice is the Prince of Lisbon.
The city stands on two islands: the main part on Sjaelland, and the smaller Christianshavn on Amager, joined by bridges.
Prince Vencel Rikard has led the city's Kindred since before the Middle Ages; once thought weak and idle, Rikard now rules firmly but fairly.
Rikard has allies or pawns across Budapest and strong friends among the Russian Kindred, and rumour says Rikard's sire moved to Russia.
Uganda offers hot savannas, thick jungles and distant mountains, with tales of strong mortal sorcerers and beings older than vampires and beyond death.
The Academy of Music and the Metropolitan Opera House entertain the elite, and many of the richest families and political figures live in the city.
Tammany Hall, run by Boss Tweed, keeps great power through illegal favours and vote-gathering, despite a setback in the 1870s.
Some groups hunt Kindred for reasons other than destruction; the Arcanum, founded within the last decade, exists to study them.
Its focus on Kindred and other supernatural beings sets it apart from general occult interest.
Among witch-hunters, inquisitors are a little likelier to have True Faith, though it is still very rare.
Lupines differ by region and people: the black-furred ones of Scandinavia are berserkers who live for battle.

The Lupines of rural Ireland and the Scottish fens are smaller and given to magic, preferring a mystical ambush to an open fight; American Lupines lean more toward the spiritual and share many customs with native peoples.

title: Tainted Places
summary: Where madness and sickness soak into the world.

claims.text: In some places madness clings to the ground, and those who enter start to break down in mind and feeling; escape is often harder than it sounds.
Disease too can seep into the world, and a truly vile one might even drive its victims like puppets.
Characters are built as in Vampire: The Masquerade: seven dots to the primary Attributes, five to the secondary and the rest to the tertiary, then Abilities ranked the same way.
Ability dots only measure dice against other characters; they should not decide a story through period trivia.
